correctness.rationale: The actual bracket equations a_i b_{i+1}-a_{i+1} b_i=0 show that nontrivial adjacent support runs impose one-dimensional common-ratio constraints, adjacent unsupported positions are zero, and isolated support coordinates stay free. Distinct resulting kernels correspond to canonical run-zero output descriptions plus projective line ratios. The seven-state determinized support-output automaton is weighted by q−1 for each B-run continuation. Independently recomputed its symbolic resolvent e0(I-u M)^(-1)h, exactly matching the stated rational generating function for formal u. Additionally enumerated literal row-reduced finite-field edge-bracket matrices over F2 up to n=10 and F3 up to n=7, deduplicating kernels, and all counts equal matrix powers; finite checks complement but do not replace all-n automaton proof.

originality.rationale: The invariant is the count of different embedded centralizer subspaces, not the distribution of their dimensions, counts of elements, or isomorphism types. Rossmann (2022) counts group conjugacy classes by orbit size, including an explicit path class polynomial; its class number does not count equality classes of centralizer kernels. Published broader graphical Lie algebra rank spectra and isomorphism-type descriptions omit projective ratio data needed for this count. No exact matching rational generating function was found in Resultary queries; historical priority risk remains.

value.rationale: Counting distinct actual centralizers (rather than their dimensions) is a natural structural invariant of finite graphical Lie algebras. Seven-state canonicalization and the exact rational length series give a nontrivial all-path classification across finite fields, with q-dependent projective parameters.

scientific_limitations: Only distinct embedded element-centralizer subalgebras for paths with independent central edge brackets, including characteristic 2, not arbitrary labeled graphs or isomorphism-class counts.
Finite rowspace enumerations are independent checks of small instances; all-n claim rests on canonical support description and automaton.
